classification.difficultyReason: Model both base dimensions after corner cuts, solve the resulting quadratic and reject the geometrically impossible root.

content.prompt:
Use a quadratic equation to solve the problem. Clearly define any pronumerals introduced into your solution.

A piece of sheet metal measuring $50\text{ cm}\times40\text{ cm}$ has squares cut out of each corner so that it can be bent and formed into an open box (with no lid) with a base area of $1344\text{ cm}^2$. Find the dimensions of the box.

answer.short:
$42\text{ cm}\times32\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ (length × width × height).

Each corner square has side length $4\text{ cm}$; subtract twice this length from each sheet dimension.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ cm be the side length of each corner square. The box has height $x$ cm and base dimensions $(50-2x)$ cm and $(40-2x)$ cm, with $0<x<20$.

$$\begin{align*}(50-2x)(40-2x)&=1344\\4x^2-180x+2000&=1344\\4x^2-180x+656&=0\\x^2-45x+164&=0\\(x-4)(x-41)&=0\\x&=4\text{ or }x=41\end{align*}$$

Reject $x=41$ because the corner squares would be too large for the sheet.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Length}&=50-2(4)=42\text{ cm}\\\text{Width}&=40-2(4)=32\text{ cm}\\\text{Height}&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

Hence the box measures $42\text{ cm}\times32\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$. Its base area is $42\times32=1344\text{ cm}^2$.
